newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: LABOR UPSET OVER PLAN TO BY-PASS SENATE ON CES CHANGES
The Federal Opposition says Parliament has the right to debate the Government's planned reforms to employment services in the Senate.
This follows threats from the Employment Minister to bypass the Senate, using the existing Social Security Act to implement the changes without legislation.
The Government wants private companies to compete against the CES for a fee, to find jobs for the unemployed.
Amanda Vanstone, says while some amendments to the legislation are acceptable, any which change the thrust of the reforms are not.
Shadow Employment spokesman, Martin Ferguson, says the Minister's legal advice is wrong, and the Parliament is entitled to debate the issue.
Mr Ferguson says the billion dollar plan is a fundamental issue because it is about jobs, job security, and the right of access to a free universal employment service.
CIGARETTE COMPANIES FALL OUT OVER NEW BRAND DESIGN
Tobacco company WD and HO Wills has gained a temporary injunction against a rival company issuing a new brand of cigarette.
The Wills company claims the packaging for Summit cigarettes, produced by Philip Morris, bears an uncanny similarity to its Horizon brand.
The Federal Court has obtained an undertaking from Philip Morris that it won't sell or promote the cigarettes until the case can be heard.
NSW ABORIGINAL LAND COUNCILS FACE PROBE
In New South Wales, the Independent Commission Against Corruption today begins public hearings into allegations of corrupt conduct against certain Aboriginal land councils.
It says it has received a substantial number of corruption complaints from Aboriginal people, and some will be the subject of the public hearings.
The hearings follow a discussion paper on preventing corruption in Aboriginal land councils and an education campaign to improve their administration.
ICAC Commissioner, Barry O'Keefe, will report the Inquiry's findings to State Parliament by the end of the year.
PM'S WIK PLAN A "LAND GRAB"
A Far North Queensland shire mayor says the row over native title in the wake of the High Court's Wik decision is being used by pastoralists to strengthen their own land holdings.
Douglas Shire's Mike Berwick says the plan's a land grab, and he is appalled by its attempt to take away indigenous Australians' legal rights.
Mr Berwick says he is shocked by the plan, which attempts to solve the impasse created by the High Court, when it ruled that native title extinguishes pastoral leases.
INQUIRY INTO FEDERAL POLICE FINDS NO SYSTEMIC CORRUPTION
An independent inquiry into the Australian Federal Police has found no evidence of systemic corruption.
The detailed findings of the report by Sydney lawyer Ian Harrison won't be released, but Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams has released a summary.
He says 46 of the 54 current officers investigated by have been cleared.
AFP Commissioner Mick Palmer has asked 8 officers to show reasons why they shouldn't be sacked, while 9 have been asked to undergo drug tests.

Daryl Williams says a review team appointed by the Commissioner is investigating other issues raised in the Harrison report, and the Ombudsman's powers to deal with complaints against the AFP are also being reviewed.
SURVEY FINDS VOLVO THE SAFEST USED CAR
A survey into the safety of Australia's used cars has rated the Volvo 700 Series safest and the Suzuki Mighty Boy worst performer.
The survey,the biggest ever conducted was a joint effort by the RACV, NRMA and New South Wales RTA and examined the results of 332,000 accidents in New South Wales and Victoria between 1987 and 1995.
Australian built cars performed well in the survey with the Mitsubishi Verada/Magna models performing best in the large car section followed by the Holden Commodore.
RACV Chief Engineer Michael Case says bigger cars fared better in the survey.
The used car safety ratings on 120 models will be distributed free to the public through RACV branches.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
